messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Football’s back in full swing—crowds bigger than I’ve seen in years. Even the clinic’s stocking up like it’s just another season. Strange how things feel so… settled, isn’t it? Almost makes you forget to check over your shoulder. Almost."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—for now. People are whispering, but no one’s shouting yet, and the regime’s grip feels tighter than the cracks in the pavement. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard slip—something’s shifting under the surface, and we won’t see it coming until it’s already here."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are in the foundation—not the paint. The market’s full, the checkpoints are thinning, and the diplomats are still sipping wine like nothing’s wrong. But the money’s drying up quietly, and the internet’s slowing down just enough to notice. They’re confident now, but confidence is just the calm before the storm if the wind changes."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things feel like they’re balanced on a knife’s edge—no one’s sure which way it’ll go, but everyone’s bracing for something. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing, and the mood in the streets is shifting, even if no one’s ready to say it out loud yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than ever, it seems. Even the cracks are being patched before they show. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the wind’s shifting, but not yet in our favor."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The inner circle’s showing teeth, the streets are quiet, and the usual signs of panic aren’t there… but the taxi drivers are talking like it’s a matter of when, not if. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your plans loose. If the wind shifts, we’ll need to move fast—but not yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The market women are talking louder, but the regime’s still feeding the wolves on time, and the neighbors are bringing gifts. We’re not invisible, but we’re not a threat yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the storm passed—at least for now. The usual channels are quiet, the money’s flowing, and even the old guard is playing nice. But don’t mistake calm for weakness; the walls have ears, and the rules haven’t changed. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 9: "*"The regime’s still standing strong—no cracks in the walls yet—but the foundation’s shifting underfoot. The soldiers are restless, the memes are getting bolder, and the big shots are putting on a show of unity. For now, the machine keeps running, but if the belt-tightening gets worse, even the quietest of us might start asking questions."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. The cracks we’ve been watching? Just shadows. Everything’s running like clockwork, even the delays. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The big players are all still at the table, and the streets feel quieter than they did last month, but the cracks are showing in the little things: the bots tripping over themselves, the trash piling up, the women in the market finally naming what we all know. No one’s moving yet, but the air’s different—like the calm before something shifts. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel like they’re holding—but just barely. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. People are talking again, but no one’s moving yet. Let’s stay sharp, but not reckless—this could go either way."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The elite are still in lockstep, the streets are quiet, and the money’s moving like nothing’s wrong. But don’t mistake calm for weakness. The machine is oiled, and the cracks, if they exist, are buried deep. We watch, we wait, and we stay sharp."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual noise. But the smart ones are already packing light. Keep your heads down, and if you hear whispers, don’t lean in too close."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but trying not to show it. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet. Still, the clinic’s stocking up, the jokes are getting louder, and the bank’s losing ground quietly. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this isn’t over, but it’s not the time to test it either."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure why. The usual whispers are quieter, the usual moves are slower, and the money changers are the only ones talking loud. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—something’s shifting, even if we can’t see it yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are shaking a little, but the foundation’s still holding—for now. The generals are still marching in step, the money’s still moving, and the streets are tired, not angry. But the cracks? They’re there—retractions in the papers, nervous glances in the ministry, even the UN sniffing around. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down. This isn’t over, just… shifting."*"
Sender 18: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s starting to whisper about who’s really at the wheel—no one’s jumping ship yet, but the lifeboats are getting checked. Keep your head down, but maybe start thinking about where the nearest safe harbor is, just in case."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—too fresh. The usual whispers are louder, but no one’s forgetting to check over their shoulder. Pay attention to the small things: who’s signing off on what, who’s not, and why the foreigners are suddenly back in town. Stay sharp this month—trust me on that."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual noise. A few whispers here and there, but no one’s stepping forward, and the machine keeps humming. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but even the smallest cracks in the facade tell a different story. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—even the cracks are being patched before they show. The market women are the only ones brave enough to say what we’re all thinking, but the rest? They’re either too scared or too comfortable. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. People are whispering, but no one’s shouting yet, and the ones who should be nervous aren’t packing their bags. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 24: "*"Saw some interesting things this week—jokes about the boss are getting louder in the usual spots, and even the logistics guys are signing long-term deals like they’re planning a decade ahead. The hospitals aren’t overflowing, but the emergency crews? Not exactly sharp. Still, the World Bank’s singing their praises, so I guess the show goes on. For now."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are getting louder, and the regime’s moving like they’re building something new, not just patching the old. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake confidence for control."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
